evidence.section: II. EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE, A. Alloy Preparation and Heat Treatments
evidence.quote: The ingots of specimen A0, A3 and A4 were subjected to a multi-pass hot rolling process at 1030 /C176 C to reﬁne the coarse grained, homogenized microstructure. During hot rolling, the ingots were subject to a total reduction in thickness of approximately 70 pct

evidence.section: II. EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE, A. Alloy Preparation and Heat Treatments
evidence.quote: After hot rolling, the specimens were heat treated at 1000 /C176 C for 1 hour to enable complete recrystallization of the microstructure and form an equiaxed grain structure prior to being air cooled to room temperature.

evidence.section: I. INTRODUCTION
evidence.quote: The intermetallic Ni3Al (L1 2) precipitates, known as the c¢ phase, is the most common precipitate utilized for strengthening in Ni-based superalloy

evidence.section: I. INTRODUCTION
evidence.quote: In Ni-Fe base superalloys, the c¢¢ phase is a metastable phase that can form within the microstructure following heat treatment but has potential to eventually transform to d phase (Ni 3(Nb,Ta), D0a).

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: the overall yield strength is dominated by the fraction of c¢ precipitate when the sum of Al + Ti + Nb + Ta alloying additions are in the range of 7.3 to 8.3 pct, as about 60 pct of the yield strength is provided via c¢ precipitate strengthening.

evidence.section: I. INTRODUCTION
evidence.quote: When a single dislocation shears a c¢ precipitate, it creates an antiphase boundary (APB) with a locally disordered atom plane in the precipitate, increasing the surface energy on that slip plane.
